rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Molecules of every body are in ceaseless random motion; their total kinetic and potential energies make up **thermal energy**. **Temperature** measures the *average* translational kinetic energy ($\bar{KE} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$) — an intensive quantity in kelvin that decides the direction of heat flow.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Heat ≠ temperature:** heat is energy in transit (J); temperature is average molecular KE (K).  ·  **Bodies don't 'contain heat'** — they contain internal energy; heat describes the transfer.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The zeroth law says that if each of two bodies is in equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other. That is what makes a thermometer possible.  ·  Absolute zero is 0 K, about −273°C, where the classical molecular picture reaches its lowest energy.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Sparkler vs bathtub*** — a 1000 °C spark has tiny energy; a 40 °C bathtub scalds — temperature ≠ energy.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short (2m): A red-hot nail and a bucket of warm water — which has more thermal energy? Which has higher temperature?** — The nail has higher temperature; the bucket of water (much larger mass) has more thermal energy. Temperature is intensive, energy extensive.

rows.text: 2.5 Distinguish heat vs temperature (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024) · Heat | Temperature · Form of energy in transit | Degree of hotness (average molecular KE) · Unit: joule | Unit: kelvin · Depends on mass, material, temperature change | Independent of mass · Measured by calorimeter | Measured by thermometer · Flows due to ΔT | Determines flow direction · Additive (extensive) | Not additive (intensive)

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Intensive vs extensive:** temperature is intensive (independent of size); heat/thermal energy is extensive (scales with mass).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Temperature ∝ average translational KE; heat flows hot → cold due to ΔT.  ·  Units: heat — joule; temperature — kelvin.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Absolute zero (0 K = −273.15 °C) is the temperature of minimum possible molecular kinetic energy.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Heat flows → B  ·  Temperature of an ideal gas tracks → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Two Words That Are Not Synonyms "Heat" and "temperature" are used interchangeably in daily speech — and wrongly in physics. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of molecules; heat is energy *in transit* because of a temperature difference.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 Molecular concept of thermal energy Matter is made of particles in ceaseless random motion. **Thermal energy** is the total internal energy of these particles — kinetic (translation, rotation, vibration) plus potential (intermolecular).…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 44:** thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law formalise "no net heat flow". - **To Kinetic theory (Unit 13):** $\bar{KE} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$ makes temperature molecular. - **To Quantity of heat (Unit 11):** Q = mcΔT quantifies heat.
